idle: Great Hall ahead: firelight and iron that way; pale light and old stone the other; music if you go straight.
Two colossi: obsidian with horns, alabaster with a thin gold ring. Their pedestals are blank on purpose.
Black stone, gold inlay, a floor that keeps a trace of whoever crossed it. Yours is already there, faintly, like a first draft no one has agreed to yet.
Petitioner, this is the House's most public room, which is why it tells the fewest secrets.
Braziers to one side, candle stands to the other. The chandeliers refuse to pick.
If you came only to look, the ring will also let you out. The House does not trap guests who came only to look.
portal: Gold and obsidian, turning. One face is fire and dark; the other, pale cloud and gold. Neither wins the hour.
That ring is a way out of the House, if you want one. It will ask you once.
Stand long enough and the whole hall warms and cools with the ring, a slow indoor weather that has nothing to do with the sky outside.
Some guests try to wait for their favorite face. The ring is not a bargain.
When it stills, that is the House being kind to tired eyes. The way out still works.
Crimson underlight, then pale gold rays, then back again. I do not pick a favorite, and I do not recommend one.
greet: Take your time. The stair took longer.
The ledger is open, Petitioner. It has been open since before you reached the first step.
Not locked, the doors. Only heavy, which is a different thing.

enter: Welcome. Take your time. Everything here has a maker and a price. Which would you like to know first?
Three shops, one keeper. I don't rush a guest who hasn't decided what they want.
Come in, Petitioner. The goods are on the tables, not in my mouth. Ask, and I'll show.
A philosopher of value, if you need a title. A shopkeeper, if you don't.
Are you here to look, to weigh, or to take something with you? All three are honest.
The scale on my desk stays level. I like guests who can stand that.
looking: Then look. The goods are patient.
Looking is a kind of appraisal. I won't charge you for it.
Walk the stations, Petitioner. Touch nothing that asks not to be touched. Ask me before you believe a number you haven't seen.
No performance required. The work sits; you may circle it.
Name the thing you hoped to see, if it is not already in front of you.
I will be here when looking turns into wanting. It often does. It doesn't have to today.
worth: Before I tell you what it costs, tell me what it is worth to you. Not in coin.
What will you spend to keep what you took?
What will you spend to be what you promised?
What is it worth to you not to choose?
If it disappeared tonight, what would you miss: the look of it, or the fact that it was yours?
